solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl is attached to it but what's its name!

indicators.note: the girl's name is fixed on after the word for it, so it follows

parts.note: 'it' as a noun stands for an object, a thing
Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker can't recall what a girl is fastened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatsit or thingummy is a placeholder word used when a name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Not fully entertained when president first proclaimed

indicators.note: the president's name is placed at the front of the charade

parts.note: Donald Trump, US president

indicators.note: the word for entertained is incomplete, losing its opening letter

parts.note: feted means entertained lavishly

explanation.surface: Someone was half-heartedly hosted while the president took precedence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fully' removes the opening letter of the word for entertained; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it loudly, as a herald's instrument would.

clue.text: Irish admit new nurse who provides security

indicators.note: the Irish letters let the rearranged word in between them
the nurse is made new, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish hospital takes on a fresh nurse to keep everyone safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish' looks like an adjective for the nurse, but it supplies the two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwriter offers financial cover against loss, a kind of security.

clue.text: Put up large wager on where old felon's last station may be

definitions.text: where old felon's last station may be

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for large is set upward, read from bottom to top

parts.note: big means large
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a big bet on where a criminal ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns BIG into GIB in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanged criminals were displayed on a gallows-like post, their final place of exhibition.

clue.text: Timers attached to dam repositioned away from the banks

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are moved to new places

explanation.surface: Timing devices fixed to a dam have been moved somewhere else.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a river lies furthest from either shore.

clue.text: Urge party to give consent

parts.note: LIB is short for the Liberal party
saying 'I do' gives consent at a wedding

explanation.surface: A call for a political party to agree to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual desire is a strong drive or appetite.

clue.text: A politician gripped by crazy parody

indicators.note: the A and politician are held inside the word for crazy

parts.note: loon is a crazy person
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician held by a madman makes a mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirical send-up imitates its target to ridicule it.

clue.text: Annual dinner to appeal most to vegans?

definitions.text: Annual dinner to appeal most to vegans?

parts.words: Annual dinner to appeal most to vegans?
parts.note: an employer's yearly celebration meal, whose name suggests a banquet of pulses that plant eaters would love

explanation.surface: Which yearly feast would best please those who eat no animal products?
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British works outing or annual celebration dinner is called this.

clue.text: Romantic poet accepting the old leading lady

indicators.note: the poet's name takes in the archaic word

parts.note: John Donne, poet of love verse
ye is an old form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A love poet welcoming the actress of former days.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior and most respected woman in a field is its foremost figure.

clue.text: See 12
Seventies rock band no-one should be seen with

definitions.meaning: the English rock group formed in 1973
undesirable associates you would be wise to avoid

explanation.definitionFit: The group's name also describes disreputable people one should not associate with.

clue.text: Cigar producing a flawless smoke ring

parts.note: perfect means flawless
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cigar that blows a perfect smoke ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of cigar thick in the middle and tapered at both ends.

clue.text: Don't start undressing until some future time

indicators.note: the word for undressing loses its first letter

parts.note: doffing clothes is taking them off

explanation.surface: Advice to wait before stripping off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something 'in the offing' is likely to happen soon, at a later point.

clue.text: Surprises that come with some trousers!

definitions.meaning: folded-up cuffs at the bottom of trouser legs

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an unexpected happening, and also the folded cuffs on trousers.

clue.text: Band earn a fresh side order

indicators.note: the letters are made afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Musicians earn a new extra dish with their curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian flatbread commonly ordered on the side with a curry.

clue.text: Described badly; need detail

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a disordered way

explanation.surface: Someone has done a poor job of describing and must add specifics.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline or portray something in words is to depict it precisely.

clue.text: Essential job description for Winnie!

parts.note: the name Winnie holds the word for a pub at its heart, so it 'keeps' a tavern

explanation.surface: A neat summary of what Winnie the Pooh or a woman named Winnie does.
explanation.walkthrough: W-INN-IE has an INN at its core, so the name itself is a keeper of an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who runs a pub or tavern for travellers.

clue.text: Protestor will infiltrate Norfolk town first

indicators.note: the town comes at the front

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England
to enter a place, as an infiltrator does

explanation.surface: An activist plans to sneak into a Norfolk town ahead of others.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who objects to established views or doctrine is a protester.

clue.text: Specks of dirt everywhere below stairs; it's a disgrace

indicators.note: only a speck, the first letter, of each of the two words is taken

parts.note: the basement lies below the stairs, servants' quarters

explanation.surface: Grime all over the servants' quarters is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering something in esteem or quality is a degradation.

clue.text: He absolves ten in rescue tragedy

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the jumbled letters
the rescue goes disastrously wrong, its letters jumbled

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten people died in a failed rescue, but someone forgives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragedy' rearranges RESCUE into ECUSER, with X going 'in' after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pardons or lets another off is one who forgives.

clue.text: What keeps the place warm before soldiers enter?

definitions.text: What keeps the place warm before soldiers enter?

parts.words: What keeps the place warm before soldiers enter?
parts.note: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, which a knitted cover keeps hot

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how a barracks is heated before troops arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin fingers of toast for dipping into a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cover placed over a boiled egg to keep it hot at the breakfast table.

clue.text: Cast of sots?

parts.note: rearranging the letters of a word meaning flip, with '...' as the signal, makes these drunkards

explanation.surface: A troupe of drunkards in a play?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, the answer says 'shuffle TOSS', which gives SOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast someone away is to expel or reject them.

clue.text: The last is just United

parts.note: only means just
one means united, as in 'all one'

explanation.surface: A football fan proclaims that the final word is simply United.
explanation.definitionFit: The final remaining item is the sole survivor of its kind.

clue.text: Individual given new second calling

indicators.note: the word for individual has its second letter replaced

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: A person handed a fresh second career.
explanation.walkthrough: The second letter E becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar's vocation to the ministry stands for the clergyman who holds it.

clue.text: Two reserves for the cooler

parts.note: frozen water and a pouch, two things kept in reserve to chill an injury; also ice and bag both mean reserve

explanation.surface: A pair of substitutes headed for the sin bin.
explanation.walkthrough: To put something on ice and to bag a seat are both ways to reserve, so the two words together name the cold pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouch of frozen cubes applied to cool an injury.

clue.text: 40% of delegation toured his old country to find president

indicators.note: the four letters travel round the old country
four of the ten letters, taken from the front

parts.note: Gaul was the ancient name of the region that became France

explanation.surface: Part of a delegation travelled round the land a leader once knew.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty per cent of a ten-letter word is its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles, French wartime leader, later headed the Fifth Republic.

clue.text: Old word processors having misleading notes on models

indicators.note: the notes are led astray into a new order

parts.note: types are models or patterns

explanation.surface: Vintage word processors come with confusing notes about their models.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand machines that court reporters once used to record speech.

clue.text: See 20
The guy you need when assistance is required one day

definitions.text: The guy you need when assistance is required

explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe's servant gave the name 'man Friday' to any trusty helper; it is also a weekday.

clue.text: Under a new regime, monarch is without splendour

indicators.note: the monarch's letters lie outside the rearranged ones

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: the letters are put under fresh rule, rearranged

explanation.surface: A king loses his pomp after a political change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under a' looks like part of the phrase 'under a new regime', but it is the anagram fodder; GR is King George's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence and impressive grandness of appearance.
